open_prs.title: fix(pi-launch): fall back to the running host CLI when no pi is on PATH
open_prs.author: tickernelz

commits.message:
fix(pi-launch): fall back to the running host CLI when no pi is on PATH

resolvePiLaunch() assumed a standalone `pi` executable on PATH for every
non-Windows host, so delegate, Fusion, and attested runs failed with
ENOENT wherever the CLI is not installed globally: npx invocations,
project-local installs, and rebranded hosts that ship the same agent under
another binary name.

The process that loads this extension is itself a Pi CLI, so it can launch
the child. A standalone `pi` on PATH still wins; only when none is found do
we resolve the running host script (process.argv[1]) and spawn it through
process.execPath, the same package-node-cli shape Windows already uses.

The launcher symlink usually carries no file extension, so the script is
realpath-resolved before the node entry-point check, and resolution still
fails closed when neither route yields a JavaScript entry point.

PATH is injectable so resolution stays deterministic under test: the
existing POSIX case previously passed only because npm prepends
node_modules/.bin, which contains a `pi` shim.

Tests: pi present -> bare path form; pi absent -> host-self form; neither
-> pi_executable_resolution_failed. Without the change the two new cases
fail. Full unit suite 444/444, docs regenerated and docs:verify clean.

open_prs.title: fix(pi-launch): locate the Pi manifest from the running host script on Windows
open_prs.author: boggylp

commits.message:
🤖: fix(pi-launch): locate the Pi manifest from the running host script on Windows

When Pi is installed globally and this package sits in Pi's extension
prefix, module resolution from the package cannot reach
@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/package.json and every child Pi launch
fails with pi_executable_resolution_failed. The running host script
(process.argv[1]) lives inside the Pi package, so after both module
lookups fail, walk up from it to the nearest named package.json and
accept it only when its name is the Pi package. The manifest then feeds
the unchanged bin, realpath, containment, and extension checks.

reviews.body:
### 🟢 Approval recommended The Windows-only fallback preserves fail-closed validation semantics and is covered by targeted new unit tests for both success and rejection paths.
Pull request overview This PR fixes Windows `resolvePiLaunch()` failures when Pi is installed globally and `pi-background-tasks` is loaded from Pi’s extension prefix, by adding a fallback that locates the Pi package manifest via the running host script path when module-based resolution cannot see Pi’s global install. **Changes:** - Extend Windows manifest resolution to fall back to walking upward from the host script (`process.argv[1]` / injected `hostScript`) to find the nearest named `package.json` matching `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. - Add unit tests covering the new fallback (including skipping nameless sub-manifests and failing closed for foreign host scripts). - Update durability/safety and troubleshooting docs to describe the new Windows resolution behavior and error shape.

open_prs.title: fix(core): stop retrying terminal publication into a closed EventBus
open_prs.author: erikdarlingdata

commits.message:
fix(core): stop retrying terminal publication into a closed EventBus

handleTerminalPublishFailure rescheduled every failed terminal publish
after 100ms, gated only on !task.terminalPublished. That flag can never
become true once the EventBus service is closed, because publishTerminal
throws before it is set -- so the handler re-armed itself indefinitely,
logging a full stack trace roughly ten times a second for the life of
the pi process. unref() keeps the timer from holding the process open at
exit, but the process is long-lived, and the timer belongs to the
previous activation's registry, so /reload cannot clear it: the terminal
floods until the process is killed.

The closed-bus state is reachable in ordinary use. session_shutdown
closes the service in its finally block, while the same handler drives
running tasks terminal, and a gated publish (fusion tasks build a
terminalPublicationGate) can resolve after the close.

Treat a closed bus as terminal instead: log once and give up, mirroring
the shuttingDown short-circuit notifyCompletion already has. Setting
terminalPublished is what ends the loop, since every publish path checks
it; it means 'no further attempts', not 'delivered'. Transient failures
keep their existing retry, which the pre-existing coverage still pins.

Adds regression tests for both guard arms (closed-bus message and
shuttingDown), each asserting no re-arm after 350ms -- well past the
100ms retry interval.

Fixes #24
